name: Derayah Financial
legal_name: Derayah Financial Company (a Saudi Joint Stock Company)
founded: 2009 (CMA licence 08109-27 dated 16 Jun 2008 per financial statements; commenced business 1 Jul 2009; commercial registration dated 29 Apr 2009)
ownership_summary: Listed on the Saudi Exchange Main Market on 10 Mar 2025 (ticker 4084, ISIN SA1690F1VQ15) after a secondary offering of 49,947,039 existing shares (20% of 249.74m shares) at SAR 30 by pre-IPO shareholders; the company received no proceeds and the pre-IPO holders' stake fell from 100% to 80%. At 31 Dec 2025 holders of 5% or more were Taha AlKuwaiz 19.25%, Abdulaziz Ibrahim Al Jammaz & Brothers Co. 7.58%, Sand Investment Company 7.35% and Al Touq Company Limited 5.44%. Free float 38.2% and foreign ownership 7.67% at 31 Dec 2025 (annual report 2025, p.15).

shareholders.holder: Abdulaziz Ibrahim Al Jammaz & Brothers Co.

government_link: No state shareholder among the 5%+ holders listed at 31 Dec 2025 (S9). Chairman Taha AlKuwaiz formerly chaired Saudi Tadawul Group Holding (2011-2014) and was Vice Chairman of STC (2016-2019); CEO sits on the CMA Financial Market Institutions Committee (since 2022) (S9).
group_structure: Derayah Financial Company is the single CMA-licensed operating entity (custody, advising, arranging, dealing, managing investments, operating funds) with branches in Dammam and Jeddah. Consolidated subsidiaries are two funds: Derayah Gulf Real Estate Fund (100% unitholding, SAR 74m) and, since 4Q 2025, the Derayah Trading Finance Fund (margin-financing fund, consolidated with no direct investment by the company). Derayah Technology Services (Egypt, 99.5%, IT services) is not consolidated. D360 Bank is a 20.4% associate (equity method); expected to fall to about 16.35% after D360's SAR 1.5bn capital raise in which Derayah commits SAR 100m (S5).

footprint: Saudi Arabia (Riyadh head office; Dammam and Jeddah branches, S8). Clients access 46 local, regional and global markets (5 local, 10 regional, 31 global per the 2Q 2026 investor presentation). Checked 2026-10-12.
customer_segments: Saudi retail investors (about 100% online acquisition, 23% of accounts aged 30 or under, 45% aged 30-40 at 2Q 2026), active traders, margin clients, growing institutional brokerage (testing phase), HNW and family offices via discretionary and advisory services; foreign investors and GCC residents are a stated growth target (S6).
business_lines: Brokerage (Derayah platform for Saudi and regional markets, Derayah Global for international markets, margin financing, Stock Yield Enhancement Program securities lending); asset management (public and private-market funds, discretionary portfolios, REIT, 42-fund third-party supermarket); digital wealth (Derayah SMART robo-advisory); investment advisory for HNW and institutions; strategic investments (D360 Bank, Alpaca and others).

capabilities.wealth_summary: Derayah says it is Saudi Arabia's largest independent digital broker (14% overall local plus international brokerage share, trailing 12 months to 1Q 2026), with 660,000 client accounts, SAR 36.9bn of assets under custody and SAR 21.8bn of AUM at 30 Jun 2026. Its shelf covers Saudi equities (zero commission since 18 Jan 2026), 46 markets through Derayah Global, margin financing, securities lending (SYEP), the Derayah SMART robo-advisor (Shariah-compliant, 0.65% fee, from SAR 500), a 42-fund third-party supermarket, in-house public and private-market funds (nine launched in 2025), discretionary portfolios from SAR 50m and investment advisory for HNW clients and institutions. Strategy 2030 targets 1.1m accounts, about 3x AUM versus 2025 and SAR 8bn of wealth AUM, with SMART relaunched for mass retail and a 'HENRY' offer for affluent and HNW clients. The platform is mostly built in-house with open-API partners (Alpaca investment; Abyan, Tamra, Joa integrations) and a 20.4% stake in D360 Bank for banking cross-sell.

asset_management.detail: AUM SAR 21.8bn at 30 Jun 2026 (SAR 22.5bn at 31 Dec 2025; 75% public market, 25% private market at 1H 2026), blended yield 52bps. Public funds include Freestyle Saudi Equity, GCC Growth and Income, Saudi Equity, Opportunistic Saudi Equity, Nomu Market, a money market fund and Derayah REIT; private funds cover credit, real estate, venture and private equity. Nine funds launched in 2025; pipeline of about SAR 1.5bn real estate and SAR 750m alternative funds over the next 9-12 months (as of 4 Aug 2026). Strategy 2030 targets about SAR 52bn AM AUM.

brokerage.detail: CMA licence 08109-27. Local and online brokerage (Saudi equities, zero commission since 18 Jan 2026, margin, Stock Yield Enhancement Program), regional and global brokerage via Derayah Global (46 markets; US stocks and ETFs, options, futures, bonds; zero US commission since 2024), plus a testing-phase institutional desk. Traded value SAR 447bn in FY2025 and SAR 266bn in 1H 2026.

digital_investing.detail: Derayah app (single unified app being built, 'Derayah Wealth' and 'Derayah Pro' personas) and web platform; about 100% online client acquisition; onboarding activation cut from 2 days to about 2 minutes; Derayah SMART standalone robo app.

advisory.detail: Investment Advisory: tailored asset allocation, independent fund-manager selection and investment governance for HNW clients, family offices and institutions (five-step process; minimum and fees not published).

discretionary.detail: DPM from SAR 50m (value, strength, disciplined-selection strategies; team of 12 per the product page); equity portfolio management since 2012 per the company timeline.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: Derayah SMART relaunched in 2025 with a 2-fold increase in subscriptions (CEO), AUM +220% and active users 10x in 2025 (annual report). Portfolios of equities, sukuk, money market and cash: conservative 15% equities, balanced 55%, aggressive 90%; 2025 returns shown 9.44%, 15.03% and 19.80%; all Shariah-compliant.

funds_platform.detail: Mutual Funds Supermarket: 42 funds (page headline) from ANB Capital, Alistithmar, Jadwa, Osool and Bakheet, Al Rajhi Capital and SNB Capital (22 of the funds), at the managers' own fees. Strategy 2030 lists the supermarket as a product to 'fix'.

structured_products.detail: No structured notes on the shelf. Closest items are two Derayah Structured Fixed Income funds (private closed-ended funds investing in local banks' private-placement sukuk, launched Oct 2025 onwards) and sukuk IPO access.

private_markets.detail: In-house private credit (Derayah Credit Income Fund, Aug 2025), real estate (AlMaria, Tawafuq, Residential), venture capital and private equity funds (Derayah AI and Frontier Fund). Private share of AUM 25% at 1H 2026 (68% at end-2022). Expected SAR 750m of alternative funds and SAR 1.5bn of real estate funds in the next 9-12 months.

islamic_wealth.detail: Whole proposition is Shariah-oriented: SMART portfolios, new funds described as Shariah-compliant, Shariah-compliant securities borrowing and lending (market first, Aug 2025), Shariah-compliant margin and a Shariah classification of listed companies (Sep 2025).

partners.kind: Execution / brokerage infrastructure and strategic investee
partners.what: Strategic partnership and investment announced 9 Dec 2024: Alpaca provides brokerage infrastructure and open APIs for global market access, and gives foreign investors electronic access to Saudi stocks; Derayah calls its model an 'Introducing Broker' white-label brokerage capability. Alpaca raised a USD 150m Series D at USD 1.15bn post-money in 2025.
Derayah Global login redirects to an Interactive Brokers partner sign-in; no partnership statement found in text.

FY2025 results and first publication of Strategy 2030 ambitions

Announced integration of Trading Central AI research tools
2Q 2026 results: Strategy 2030 targets (1.1m accounts, about 3x AUM, about 2x operating income, 55% recurring revenue, ROAE above 42%); second interim dividend SAR 0.33 per share

opportunities: Strategy 2030 ambition of about 3x AUM, 'relaunch SMART for mass retail' and 'scale HENRY for affluent and HNW' with a stated SAR 8bn wealth AUM goal by 2030; HENRY has no public product page yet (S6 pp.32, 35).

AUM of SAR 21.8bn against AUC of SAR 36.9bn; asset management revenue fell 8% YoY in 1H 2026 on delayed fund launches, with SAR 1.5bn of real estate and SAR 750m of alternative funds planned within 9-12 months (S5 pp.3-4).
Third-party supermarket is Saudi managers only (42 funds, six houses) and Strategy 2030 lists it as a product to fix; no international managed-portfolio shelf was found (S13, S6 p.32).
Open-API model already in use: annual report cites integrations with Abyan, Tamra and Joa, and the 2Q 2026 deck lists 'productized APIs' as a capability to scale (S9 p.24, S6 p.36).
Annual report AI roadmap lists 'AI agents under exploration' and Copilot enabled for all employees (S9 p.25).
barriers: Technology is mostly in-house: a share of staff between about 30% and 50% works in IT (sources differ) and 2026-27 IT spend is front-loaded to build a unified app, data warehouse and modernised core (S6 pp.34, 36-37; S9 pp.14, 20).
Already runs its own robo (SMART, Shariah-only, 0.65% fee), DPM and advisory service; partners used for brokerage reach rather than portfolio construction (S10, S12, S14).
Saudi-regulated (CMA-licensed) and Shariah-oriented: shelf additions must fit CMA approval and Shariah screening (S9 p.8; S10).
Cost discipline: management is pairing the platform build with a minimum 60% dividend payout for FY2026-27 (S6 p.37).
